policy: Full taxonomy coverage is an index, not a publishing queue. Pages may only be generated against evidence_tier T1-T3. T4 synthetic permutations are a hypothesis reserve consulted when a cluster has no evidence, and never publish on their own.

demand_value_by_band.measured_search_volume: search_volume (monthly searches from a keyword tool)
demand_value_by_band.own_impressions_only: impressions_90d (this domain's own impressions over 90 days)
demand_value_by_band.unscored: null - no demand evidence, rank_score is null

rank_scoring.comparability: rank_score is ONLY comparable within the same rank_band. The demand term carries a different unit per band, so a cross-band comparison is a unit error. Queries are ordered by band first, then by rank_score inside the band.
rank_scoring.why: Previously one field named `volume` held monthly search volume on semrush rows and this domain's own 90-day impressions on GSC rows, and rank_score was computed from it directly. That made a 1,300/mo KD-9 query score ~35x below a 320/mo query. Splitting the field and banding the score removes the comparison entirely.

unit_contract.search_volume: Monthly searches reported by a keyword tool. null when unknown.
unit_contract.impressions_90d: This domain's own impressions over the measured 90-day GSC window. null when unknown.
unit_contract.demand_basis: Which field rank_score used: search_volume | impressions_90d | none.
unit_contract.removed_field: `volume` is removed. It previously held BOTH monthly search volume (semrush rows) and this domain's own 90d impressions (gsc rows). A missing key throws; a wrong number does not.
unit_contract.never: Do not sum or compare across units. Disagreeing packet volumes are recorded in volume_sources with volume_conflict=true and are never averaged.
unit_contract.precedent: Follows portfolio_demand.json (portfolio-demand-v1), which separated volume_mo from demand_signal/demand_signal_unit for this same defect.
